artifacts.synopsis: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.

artifacts.synopsis: A minister complained that Presbytery placed a shepherding committee report containing findings of his alleged “sins and errors” in its minutes and directed that it be read to his congregation. The SJC sustained the complaint and ordered the report expunged. Although a committee may form and record an opinion without judicial process, Presbytery's endorsement and public dissemination effectively admonished the minister on unsubstantiated and unproven opinions without due process.

artifacts.synopsis: A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. The SJC sustained the appeal: unauthorized committee citations and admonition without process could not support guilt, and multiple trial violations were fatally prejudicial. It set aside the judgment, dismissed the citation and admonition charges, and revoked both censures. The inappropriate-language charge was not adjudicated on its merits; Presbytery could retry it on remand or dismiss it.

artifacts.synopsis: A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation.

artifacts.title: Confusing use of 'admonition' in non-judicial rebuke context

matches.evidence: The CCB cautioned that using 'admonish' and 'admonition' outside their technical judicial-censure meaning in BCO 30 could cause confusion when applied to actions against church officers.

artifacts.title: Informal versus formal admonition and due-process requirements under BCO 27-5

matches.evidence: The CCB distinguished informal admonition (ordinary relational correction) from formal judicial admonition, holding that the paragraph in question did not require BCO 27-5 due process.
